Cruise findings come from CLIA, an industry trade association. Survey findings and passenger counts use different research methods.
CDC summaries sometimes combine estimates from different underlying years; summary/report labels identify publication timing rather than a common collection year.
ASPS figures estimate procedures, not unique patients. One person can receive multiple treatments. AmSpa findings are trade-association research.
Textile Exchange figures cover fibers used across apparel, home textiles, footwear, and other applications—not clothing alone.
Census construction figures describe newly completed or newly sold housing, not the entire housing stock.
BLS time-use figures are diary-based population estimates. Its 2025 release notes missing survey collection during the federal shutdown and corresponding weighting adjustments.
ESA findings come from industry-sponsored research. Player definitions generally require at least one hour of gaming per week; individual measures have their own age bases.
Figures come from the IEA’s review of 2024 unless otherwise indicated.
EPA waste figures use US short tons and refer to municipal solid waste unless otherwise stated. Reference estimates do not imply a new annual measurement.
USPS daily figures are the agency’s reported operational averages; they should not be assumed to use 365 operating days.
USDA Food Dollar figures use the revised methodology released in March 2026. Domestic-food measures exclude imported final food products unless explicitly included.
APPA findings come from trade-association research. Several 2025-report findings describe 2024 ownership and behavior.
NASA engineering specifications are reference figures; station configuration can change with upgrades and visiting vehicles.
